newsitem.title: GERMANY: German court convicts trio for "pyramid" fraud.
newsitem.headline: German court convicts trio for "pyramid" fraud.

text.p: A Frankfurt court on Tuesday convicted three founding members of a so-called "pyramid" investment club of fraud and sentenced the trio to prison terms of between 4-1/2 and seven years.

The three were accused of using their European Kings Club to cheat 94,000 participants out of 850 million marks ($560 million) in the space of four years with a scheme promising staggering annual yields of as much as 72 percent.
The Kings Club's collapsed in late 1995.

Pyramid schemes rely on existing investors recruiting ever more new members to finance the yields with their initial outlay. The schemes inevitably fail when not enough new recruits can be found to pay the returns of those higher up the pyramid.
The court convicted Harald Bertges and Andreas Rast to seven years in jail. A third defendant, Hans-Guenter Spachtholz, was sentenced to 4-1/2 years.
A separate trial for a fourth defendant, club president Damara Bertges, was continuing.
The leaders were originally charged in connection with 33,000 cases of fraud linked to 675,000 illegal bank transactions. Prosecutors used 678 model cases for the trial.
Investors had to pay 1,400 marks to join the club, an outlay which was intended to guarantee them large payouts starting with 2,400 marks in the first year.
